method: three boots, byte-identical image proven by the flash log's sha256 (their method), FWS 4 throughout because SystemInit sets it after every reset so no console knob is touched, 8 captures a boot
why_not_a_bare_reset: a software reset ('z') left the capture path dead on this bench - the console answered, the native port enumerated, and zero bytes arrived until a reflash. So the cleaner arm is not available here and the reflash form is the one that works.
verdict: NOT CONFIRMED on this bench, and not refuted either
reading: boots 0 and 1 give IDENTICAL persistent sets. A set latched per boot would not predict two consecutive boots agreeing exactly, so this is evidence against a strong per-boot latch

boot 2 is a strict SUBSET - it lost four sites and gained none. All four sat exactly AT the >=4 of 8 threshold in the earlier boots, so a small incidence change moves them across it. That is a threshold effect, not a new set
the strong sites persist across all three: 219 at 8 of 8 every boot, plus 159 and 64
limits: n=8 with a >=4 threshold is coarse, and every site that moved was sitting on the threshold. A higher n would separate 'marginal incidence' from 'absent' and this arm cannot
three boots is few, and two agreeing could still be chance
